key_insight: Selected machine-learning models outperformed average multilayer perceptron results on five of six COVID-19 outcome-prediction tasks, but performance varied substantially.
clinical_relevance: These models explore prediction of death, ICU admission, and improvement or worsening in hospitalised COVID-19 patients, without establishing readiness for clinical use.
method: Compared five classifiers: logistic regression, KNN, CART, Naive Bayes, and SVM.
Tested ANOVA, mutual information, and recursive feature elimination; selecting 20 features generally improved cross-validated accuracy.
Compared selected classifiers with multilayer perceptrons using one to five hidden layers.
evidence_signal: Two cohorts—80 Algerian and 99 French patients—were evaluated using 30 repetitions of five-fold cross-validation and separate hold-out testing; selected ML models achieved test accuracies of 0.47–0.95.
watch_item: Small, early-pandemic cohorts limit generalisability; larger independent datasets are needed before clinical use.
paper_title: Application of Machine Learning and Deep Learning in diagnosis Covid19
